questions.question:
Which of the following best describes the grammatical structure of the sentence:

"This deep connection between space and time implies that the passage of time is not universal but relative:"?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 2** i.e '**Complex sentence**'.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• A **complex sentence** consists of one independent clause and at least one dependent (subordinate) clause.
 
• In the given sentence, the **independent clause** is "This deep connection between space and time implies [something]." It can stand alone as a complete thought.
 
• The **dependent clause** is "that the passage of time is not universal but relative." This is a **noun clause** acting as the object of the verb "implies." It cannot stand alone as a complete sentence.
 
• The word **"that"** serves as the subordinating conjunction that links the dependent clause to the main independent clause.

Therefore, the **correct answer** is- **Option 2.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Simple Sentence:** Contains only one independent clause with a subject and a predicate (e.g., "Space and time are connected."). 
 
• **Compound Sentence:** Consists of two or more independent clauses joined by a coordinating conjunction (FANBOYS) or a semicolon (e.g., "Space is vast, and time is relative.").
 
• **Compound-Complex Sentence:** Contains at least two independent clauses and at least one dependent clause (e.g., "Scientists studied the data, and they concluded that time is relative.").

questions.question: What is the closest meaning of "geodesics" in the context of the passage?

options.text: Straightest possible paths in curved space-time
Circular orbits caused by gravitational pull
Fixed points of measurement in space-time

questions.solution: The correct answer is: **Option 1** i.e. straightest possible paths in curved space-time. [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__** __ • The term **"geodesics"** in the context of general relativity and curved space-time refers to the shortest or the straightest possible paths between two points in a curved space-time framework. • **Example:** In the presence of a massive object, the geodesics of space-time appear curved, though they represent the straightest possible paths in that curved geometry. • **Straightest possible paths in curved space-time** accurately captures the meaning of "geodesics," as it conveys the concept of the most direct routes within the curved space-time fabric. • The other options, such as gravitational waves, circular orbits, and fixed points of measurement, do not specifically define the shortest or direct paths described by "geodesics." Therefore, the closest meaning of "geodesics" in the context of the passage is: **straightest possible paths in curved space-time.** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__** Here are the other options and their meanings: • **Gravitational waves moving through space** (अंतरिक्ष के माध्यम से चलने वाली गुरुत्वाकर्षण तरंगें): Ripples in the fabric of space-time caused by the acceleration of massive objects. • **Circular orbits caused by gravitational pull** (गुरुत्वाकर्षण खिंचाव के कारण वृत्ताकार कक्षाएँ): Paths followed by bodies under the influence of a central gravitational force, often taking the form of elliptical or circular trajectories. • **Fixed points of measurement in space-time** (अंतरिक्ष-समय में माप के स्थिर बिंदु): Specific locations in space-time that serve as reference points for various measurements, not directly related to the concept of geodesics. 34:T720, The correct answer is **option 1.**

questions.question: In the sentence **"Gravity is no longer thought of as a force in the Newtonian sense but rather as the curvature of space-time..."**, what does the word **"curvature"** most likely refer to?

options.text: Bending of the path of planets only
Warping of the structure of space and time
Deformation of gravitational fields by energy

questions.solution:
The correct answer is '**Option 3**'.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• ***A) Defining "Curvature" in General Relativity.***

 
 
• In the context of Einstein's theory, "curvature" refers to the geometric distortion of the four-dimensional continuum. The passage explicitly links this to the "**warping of space and time itself**," replacing the Newtonian idea of gravity as a traditional force.
 
 
 
• ***B) The role of mass and energy.***
 
 
• The text states that this curvature is "caused by the presence of mass and energy." This indicates that the very fabric of the universe is what is being altered, rather than individual physical objects folding or bending independently.
 
 
 
• ***C) Influence on motion and time.***
 
 
• The passage explains that objects follow "geodesics," which are paths dictated by this warping. This confirms that curvature is a structural property of the space-time fabric that governs how everything within it moves and experiences time.
 
 

Therefore, the correct answer is **Warping of the structure of space and time.**

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 1**: Incorrect because the curvature affects the space-time fabric in which objects exist, not the "folding" of the physical objects (like rocks or ships) themselves.
 
• **Option 2**: Incorrect because the term "only" makes this statement too restrictive; curvature affects all matter, energy, and even light, not just planets.
 
• **Option 4**: Incorrect because while energy does cause the deformation, the passage defines gravity as the curvature of space-time itself, making Option 3 the most direct and accurate reflection of the text's definition.

questions.question:
Choose the correct active form of the given sentence.

Admission was refused to Sheetal by the school.

options.text: Sheetal was refused admission by the school.
The school refused admission to Sheetal.
Sheetal will be refused admission by the school.
The school has been refusing admission to Sheetal.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 2**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Active voice structure: The subject of the sentence performs the action.
 
• To convert from passive to active: Identify the agent (the one performing the action), which is "the school." This becomes the subject of the active sentence.
 
• Identify the tense: The verb phrase "was refused" indicates the **Past Simple** tense in the passive voice.
 
• The active form of the Past Simple tense is simply the past tense form of the verb, which is **"refused."**
 
• The object of the active sentence is "admission," which was the subject of the passive sentence.
 
• The recipient "Sheetal" remains as the indirect object.

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 2**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *"The school refused admission to Sheetal."*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 1:** "Sheetal was refused admission by the school." – This is still in the **passive voice**; it has simply shifted the indirect object ("Sheetal") to the subject position.
 
• **Option 3:** "Sheetal will be refused admission by the school." – This changes the tense to the **Future Simple** (passive), which alters the meaning of the original past-tense statement.
 
• **Option 4:** "The school has been refusing admission to Sheetal." – This is the **Present Perfect Continuous** tense, indicating an ongoing action rather than a completed past event.

questions.question:
Fill in the blank with the appropriate adverb.

The policy was implemented ________, without prior public consultation.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is '**arbitrarily**'.
 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**
__
 
• The word **"arbitrarily"** means something done without a specific reason or logic, often based on personal whim or impulse.
 
• The sentence suggests that the policy was implemented without prior public consultation, indicating randomness or lack of structured reasoning.
 
• **Options 2, 3,** and **4** do not fit the meaning or context of the sentence:
 
 
• **Option 2 (intuitively):** Suggests a decision based on instinct, which is unrelated to the context of the sentence.
 
• **Option 3 (pragmatically):** Indicates practicality or realism, which contradicts the idea of randomness or lack of consultation.
 
• **Option 4 (sequentially):** Implies an ordered or logical sequence, which does not align with the sentence’s meaning.
 
 

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 1**.
 
**Complete Sentence:** *"The policy was implemented **arbitrarily**__, without prior public consultation."*
 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 2 (intuitively):** Refers to decisions made based on instinct or gut feelings, not randomness.
 
• **Option 3 (pragmatically):** Refers to decisions made based on practicality or realistic considerations, which is opposite to arbitrary actions.
 
• **Option 4 (sequentially):** Refers to actions done in order or sequence, which does not describe the process mentioned in the sentence.

questions.question:
Which of the following is the correct indirect speech conversion of the given sentence?

Purna said, "Bravo! I have passed the entrance test."

options.text: Purna happily announced that she have had passed the entrance test.
Purna joyfully exclaimed that she had passed the entrance test.
Purna expressed with excitement that she had passed the entrance test.
Purna said with joy that she had passed the entrance test.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 2**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Direct Speech:** Purna said, "Bravo! I have passed the entrance test."
 
• **Key Conversions:**
 
 
• **Reporting Verb:** When the direct speech contains an exclamation like "Bravo!", it expresses joy, applause, or triumph. The reporting verb "said" is changed to "exclaimed joyfully," "exclaimed with joy," or "applauded."
 
• **"have passed" becomes "had passed"**
 
 
• The Present Perfect tense (have passed) in direct speech changes to the Past Perfect tense (had passed) in indirect speech.
 
 
 
• **Pronoun Shift:** The first-person pronoun "I" changes to the third-person "she" to match the speaker (Purna).
 
• **Conjunction:** The word "that" is used to introduce the reported clause, and the exclamatory word "Bravo!" is removed as its sentiment is captured by the reporting verb.
 
 
 
• **Punctuation and Format:**
 
 
• The exclamation mark and quotation marks are removed.
 
• The sentence ends with a full stop.
 
 

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 2**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *Purna joyfully exclaimed that she had passed the entrance test.*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 1:** "Purna happily announced that she have had passed..."

 
 
• Incorrect verb construction; "have had passed" is grammatically invalid in this context.
 
 
 
• **Option 3:** "Purna expressed with excitement that she had passed..."
 
 
• While the meaning is similar, "exclaimed joyfully" is the standard grammatical convention for reporting an exclamation like "Bravo."
 
 
 
• **Option 4:** "Purna said with joy that she had passed..."
 
 
• This is acceptable but less precise than Option 2. In competitive exams, exclamatory sentences are prioritized for conversion using the verb "exclaimed."

questions.question:
Choose the option that best expresses the same sentence in indirect speech.

I said to him, "Does your sister know French?"

options.text: I asked him whether his sister knows French.
I asked him whether his sister knew French.
I told him whether his sister knew French.
I said to him whether his sister knows French.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 2**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Direct Speech:** I said to him, "Does your sister know French?"
 
• **Key Conversions:**
 
 
• **Reporting Verb:** For interrogative sentences, the reporting verb "said to" is changed to "asked," "enquired," or "wondered." In this case, "asked" is the most appropriate choice.
 
• **Conjunction:** When a direct question begins with an auxiliary verb (like do, does, is, are, have), it is a "Yes/No" question. These are introduced by the conjunction "if" or "whether" in indirect speech.
 
• **Tense Shift:** The direct speech is in the Simple Present tense (Does... know). Since the reporting verb is in the past (said), the tense shifts to the Simple Past (knew).
 
• **Pronoun/Determiner Shift:** The possessive adjective "your" (referring to the person being spoken to, "him") changes to "his."
 
• **Word Order:** The interrogative form (Does your sister know) is converted into the assertive/statement form (his sister knew). The question mark is removed.
 
 

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 2**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *I asked him whether his sister knew French.*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 1:** "I asked him whether his sister knows French."

 
 
• Incorrect because the tense has not been shifted from present to past.
 
 
 
• **Option 3:** "I told him whether his sister knew French."
 
 
• Incorrect reporting verb; "told" is used for statements, whereas "asked" is required for questions.
 
 
 
• **Option 4:** "I said to him whether his sister knows French."
 
 
• Incorrect reporting verb and incorrect tense. "Said to" must be replaced by "asked" when a conjunction like "whether" is introduced.

questions.question:
Choose the correct active voice form from the given options.

The laptop may not be bought by her.

options.text: She may not buy the laptop.
She might not buy the laptop.
She should not have bought the laptop.
She may not have bought the laptop.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 1**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Active voice structure: The subject of the sentence performs the action of the verb.
 
• To convert from passive to active: Identify the agent (the person performing the action), which is "her." In the active voice, the pronoun "her" changes to the subject form **"She."**
 
• Identify the modal and tense: The sentence uses the modal **"may"** in a negative passive construction ("may not be bought").
 
• The active form of a modal in the present/future is "Modal + (not) + base verb." Therefore, "may not be bought" becomes **"may not buy."**
 
• The subject of the passive sentence ("The laptop") becomes the object in the active sentence.

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 1**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *"She may not buy the laptop."*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 2:** "She might not buy..." – This changes the modal from "may" to "might." While similar in meaning, the active voice should preserve the specific modal used in the original sentence.
 
• **Option 3:** "She should not have bought..." – This changes the modal to "should" and the tense to the **Past Perfect Modal** form, which expresses a missed obligation or regret.
 
• **Option 4:** "She may not have bought..." – This is the **Perfective Modal** form, which suggests a possibility about an action in the past, rather than a present/future possibility.

questions.question:
Rearrange the parts of the sentence in the correct order.

Ancient mythologies
P. while adapting to contemporary interpretations and themes
Q. influencing modern literature, cinema, and philosophy
R. preserving cultural traditions through oral storytelling
S. have transcended time and geographical boundaries,
questions.solution:
The correct answer is** Option (4)** i.e. **SQRP**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The sentence begins with "Ancient mythologies have transcended time and geographical boundaries," which is correctly indicated by **part (S).**
 
• Following the introduction, "preserving cultural traditions through oral storytelling" **(SQ)** logically continues the narrative, explaining their role in cultural preservation.
 
• **The next part,** "influencing modern literature, cinema, and philosophy" **(QR)** adds the impact of these mythologies in contemporary contexts.
 
• **Ending with **"while adapting to contemporary interpretations and themes" **(RP)** completes the sentence by highlighting their modern adaptations.

Therefore, the correct answer is **SQRP.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 1 (PRSQ):** This option starts with "while adapting to contemporary interpretations and themes preserving cultural traditions," which creates a disjointed sentence.
 
• **Option 2 (QRPS):** This option starts with "influencing modern literature, cinema, and philosophy while adapting to," which creates a fragmented sentence.
 
• **Option 3 (RPQS):** This option starts with "while adapting to contemporary interpretations and themes influencing modern literature," which breaks the logical flow.
</ul

questions.question: What does the idiom "to keep the wolf away from the door" mean?

(आर्थिक कठिनाइयों से बचने के लिए) • **Example:** He worked extra hours to keep the wolf away from the door and provide for his family. • **Explanation:** The imagery of a wolf at the door symbolizes the threat of poverty or destitution. (यह मुहावरा वित्तीय स्थिरता बनाए रखने के प्रयासों को दर्शाता है।) Therefore, the correct answer is: **Option 1** i.e. **To avoid financial hardship**. [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__** Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences: • **Option 2: To escape from a dangerous situation** (खतरनाक स्थिति से बचने के लिए) • **Example:** He jumped into the river to escape from the dangerous situation. • **Option 3: To protect oneself from enemies** (दुश्मनों से खुद को बचाने के लिए) • **Example:** The king built a strong fortress to protect himself from enemies. • **Option 4: To stay away from risky opportunities** (जोखिम भरे अवसरों से दूर रहना) • **Example:** She decided to stay away from risky opportunities to ensure stability in her career. 40:Tf10, The correct answer is **Option 1**.

questions.question:
Improve the sentence by selecting the correct form of tense from the options.

She said that she ______ the report before the deadline.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is '**had completed**'.
 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**
__
 
• The sentence refers to an action that was completed before another point in time in the past ("before the deadline").
 
• The correct tense for describing such actions is the past perfect tense, which uses the structure **"had + past participle."**
 
• **Option 1: "will complete"** is incorrect because it refers to a future action, not a past one.
 
• **Option 2: "has completed"** is incorrect because it refers to a present perfect action and does not align with the past timeline.
 
• **Option 4: "completes"** is incorrect because it suggests a habitual action rather than a completed action in the past.

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 3**.
 
**Complete Sentence:** *"She said that she **had completed**__ the report before the deadline."*
 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**
__
 
• **Past Perfect Tense:** Used to describe an action that was completed before another action in the past.
 
• **Structure:** Subject + had + past participle.
 
• **Example:** "By the time he arrived, she **had left**__."
</ul

questions.question:
Improve the sentence by selecting the appropriate tense of the underlined word.

He __work__ for an hour when I found him sleeping on the couch.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is '**was working**'.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The sentence describes an action that was in progress at a specific point in the past ("when I found him sleeping"). Therefore, the past continuous tense "**was working**" is appropriate.
 
• The past continuous tense is used to describe actions that were ongoing in the past, often interrupted by another event.
 
• **Options 1, 2**, and 3 do not match the context or the correct tense for this sentence.

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 4**.

 

**Complete Sentence:** *"He **was working**__ for an hour when I found him sleeping on the couch."*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 1: "had worked"** is incorrect because the past perfect tense implies a completed action before another past event, which doesn't fit the ongoing nature of the sentence.
 
• **Option 2: "has worked"** is incorrect because the present perfect tense describes an action completed in the past but relevant to the present.
 
• **Option 3: "will have worked"** is incorrect because the future perfect tense describes an action completed before a specific time in the future, which is irrelevant to the sentence's context.

questions.question:
Identify the error in the sentence.

Of the three runners, he was the faster.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 1**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The error lies in the use of the comparative degree "**faster**" when comparing more than two entities.
 
• In English grammar, the **comparative degree** (e.g., faster, taller, better) is used to compare **two** people or things.
 
• The **superlative degree** (e.g., fastest, tallest, best) must be used when comparing **three or more** people or things.
 
• Since the sentence specifies "**three runners**," the word "faster" should be replaced with "**fastest**."

Therefore, the correct answer is **faster**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *"Of the three runners, he was the **fastest**."*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 2: was** – This is the correct singular past tense verb agreeing with the subject "he."
 
• **Option 3: runners** – This is the correct plural noun form following the numeral "three."
 
• **Option 4: three** – This numeral adjective is used correctly to define the total number of subjects in the comparison.
 
• **Degrees of Comparison:** 
 
 
• **Positive:** fast (used for one person/thing).
 
• **Comparative:** faster (used for two people/things).
 
• **Superlative:** fastest (used for three or more people/things).

questions.question:
**Change the following from active to passive:**

The director was supposed to have finalized the script revisions before principal photography commenced.

options.text: The script revisions were supposed to have finalized by the director before principal photography commenced.
The script revisions were supposed to have been finalized by the director before principal photography commenced.
The script revisions were being supposed to have been finalized by the director before principal photography commenced.
The script revisions were supposed to being finalized by the director before principal photography commenced.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 2**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Passive voice structure: The object of the active sentence becomes the subject of the passive sentence.
 
• In the active voice, the sentence is: "The director was supposed to have finalized the script revisions..."
 
• To convert to passive voice: Place the object **"the script revisions"** at the beginning. As this is plural, the auxiliary verb changes from "was" to **"were."**
 
• The verb phrase "to have finalized" is a **perfect infinitive**. To make a perfect infinitive passive, we use the structure: **to have + been + past participle**. Thus, it becomes **"to have been finalized."**
 
• Add the preposition "by" followed by the original subject "the director."
 
• The subordinate clause "before principal photography commenced" remains unchanged.

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 2**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *"The script revisions were supposed to have been finalized by the director before principal photography commenced."*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 1:** "...supposed to have finalized..." – This keeps the perfect infinitive in the active voice, implying the revisions performed the action themselves.
 
• **Option 3:** "...were being supposed..." – This incorrectly uses the continuous form of the verb "suppose," which is a stative verb in this context and does not take the continuous aspect here.
 
• **Option 4:** "...supposed to being finalized..." – This is grammatically incorrect; the infinitive "to" should be followed by the base form "be" or the perfect "have been," not the gerund "being."
